llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Vitamin C is assumed to be solid L-ascorbic acid and is dispensed directly into the electrolyte vial as a separately identified analyte. The solution is prepared fresh immediately before electrochemical measurement because aqueous ascorbic acid is susceptible to oxidation. No pre-prepared Vitamin C solution or pre-prepared electrolyte is assumed.
assumptions: Vitamin C refers to L-ascorbic acid with molecular weight 176.12 g/mol.
Solid KCl and solid L-ascorbic acid are available for loading into Quantos cartridge positions 1 and 2, respectively.
Water is available as a pump-compatible liquid on syringe-pump channel 1.
Nitrogen is available to the electrochemical substation for the specified purge operation.
No pH adjustment is performed because no additional acid, base, or buffer component is explicitly available through the stated dispensing hardware.
The listed final volume is treated as the dispensed water volume; the volume contribution of the dissolved solid masses is neglected for the stated concentration calculations.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: Required moles = 0.100 mol/L × 0.009996 L = 0.0009996 mol. Required mass = 0.0009996 mol × 74.55 g/mol = 0.07452018 g = 74.52018 mg. This is below the 200 mg Quantos cartridge limit. Using the planned mass in 9.996 mL gives 0.100 M KCl.

Required moles = 0.00100 mol/L × 0.009996 L = 0.000009996 mol. Required mass = 0.000009996 mol × 176.12 g/mol = 0.001760496 g = 1.760496 mg. This is below the 200 mg Quantos cartridge limit. Using the planned mass in 9.996 mL gives 1.00 mM L-ascorbic acid.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: One experiment vial and one electrochemical slot are used, which are within the limits of 31 samples and 3 parallel slots. Two solids are used, within the 8-cartridge limit. Each solid mass is below the 200 mg per-cartridge Quantos limit. One liquid pump channel is used, within the 4-channel limit. The 9.996 mL water volume equals 1428 increments of 7 uL and is below the 10 mL vial limit. No solids are assigned to liquid pump channels. The electrolyte and analyte are separately identified and prepared in the experiment vial before measurement.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: Drying of a deposited analyte is not applicable because electrode deposition is disabled. The substation electrode wash-and-dry operation should be completed after polishing and before the CV run.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is used because the analyte is dissolved in the electrolyte. The gold working electrode is instead polished, washed, and dried by the electrochemical substation before immersion in the prepared solution.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense 74.52018 mg KCl from Quantos cartridge position 1 and 1.760496 mg L-ascorbic acid from Quantos cartridge position 2 into one clean experiment vial. Dispense 9.996 mL water from liquid-pump channel 1. The water volume is intentionally 9.996 mL rather than 10.000 mL because 9.996 mL is exactly compatible with the 7 uL pump increment. Mix the vial with a stir bar for 300 seconds until the solids are dissolved. Purge the mixed electrolyte with nitrogen for 300 seconds, then measure pH before starting the CV measurement and again after the final CV cycle.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.100 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte provides adequate ionic conductivity while avoiding the need for unavailable liquid buffer components. A 1.00 mM L-ascorbic acid concentration provides a readily measurable oxidation response without excessive analyte loading. The -0.10 V to +0.80 V potential window versus Ag/AgCl is selected to observe ascorbic acid oxidation on gold while beginning sufficiently negative of the expected oxidation region. A 50 mV/s scan rate, 2 mV step size, and three cycles provide initial characterization while allowing assessment of cycle-to-cycle electrode fouling or analyte depletion. The gold working electrode is polished before measurement. Nitrogen purging for 300 seconds minimizes dissolved-oxygen reduction contributions; pH is measured by the substation before and after CV.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The requested experiment requires Vitamin C to remain dissolved in the electrolyte during cyclic voltammetry; therefore, analite_in_electrolite is the applicable platform mode. Both KCl supporting electrolyte and solid L-ascorbic acid analyte are dispensed into the experiment vial using Quantos, followed by water addition through the liquid pump and mixing.

metadata.description: Characterization of dissolved Vitamin C by cyclic voltammetry in freshly prepared aqueous 0.100 M potassium chloride supporting electrolyte using a gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
metadata.experiment_name: Cyclic Voltammetry of L-Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C) in 0.100 M KCl
metadata.user_prompt: Perform a cyclic voltammetry experiment to characterize Vitamin C as an analyte dissolved in the electrolyte. The Vitamin C should be prepared in the electrolyte and measured using the electrochemical substation. Use the available gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode. Select appropriate electrolyte composition, Vitamin C concentration, CV parameters, mixing/preparation steps, and safety precautions based on the capabilities and constraints provided in the system context. The resulting experiment must be directly executable by the CVLab platform.

cross_contamination_risks: Ascorbic acid oxidation products can adsorb on the gold working electrode and alter subsequent measurements.
Chloride-containing electrolyte residue can contaminate subsequent chloride-sensitive experiments.
Use a clean experiment vial, clean stir bar, and polished/washed electrode set for this measurement.
handling_precautions: Wear laboratory coat, nitrile gloves, and safety glasses while loading Quantos cartridges and handling prepared solutions.
Avoid generating airborne L-ascorbic acid or KCl dust during cartridge loading.
Prepare the Vitamin C solution immediately before measurement and minimize air and light exposure because ascorbic acid oxidizes during storage.
Use nitrogen purge only with appropriate laboratory ventilation and ensure the gas outlet is directed safely.
Polish, wash, and dry the gold working electrode before the experiment to reduce fouling and carryover.
hazards: Potassium chloride and L-ascorbic acid are low-hazard solids, but powder exposure can cause eye or respiratory irritation.
The prepared solution is mildly acidic because of dissolved L-ascorbic acid.
Nitrogen purging can displace oxygen in poorly ventilated areas.
Electrical and mechanical hazards are present during electrode polishing and electrochemical operation.
waste_disposal: Collect the post-CV aqueous KCl/ascorbic acid solution in the designated aqueous electrochemical waste container.
Do not return used solution to reagent reservoirs.
Rinse the gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode according to platform wash procedures after measurement.
